[[Image:TU Dresden Grab Hettner u.a..jpg|thumb|Memorial Tablet to Georg Helm at the old Annenfriedhof in Dresden (Bust is of [[Hermann Hettner]]).]]

'''Georg Ferdinand Helm''' (15 March 1851 &ndash; 13 September 1923) was a German [[mathematician]].

Helm graduated from high school from the [[Annenschule (Dresden)|Annenschule]] in Dresden in 1867. Thereafter he studied mathematics and natural sciences at the Dresden Polytechnical School, and then at the universities of [[Leipzig]] and [[Berlin]] from 1871 to 1873.

Helm first taught at the Annenschule, his high school alma mater.<ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=3vEXanhpFQUC&dq=liesske+annen&pg=PA42 Programm der Annen-Realschule zu Dresden 1882, page 50]</ref>  Then he taught [[mathematics]] and [[physics]] at the Royal Saxon Polytechnic (now [[Dresden University of Technology|TU Dresden]]) from 1888 until 1922.   He was an interdisciplinarian, whose teaching responsibilities included a seminar on insurance statistics.   Helm coined the term “[[mathematical chemistry]]”, and was the first to classify physical and chemical properties as [[intensive and extensive properties|intensive or extensive]] in 1898.<ref name="Redlich">{{cite journal | title=Intensive and Extensive Properties | author=Redlich, O. | journal=J. Chem. Educ. | year=1970 | volume=47 | issue=2 | pages=154–156 | doi=10.1021/ed047p154.2|bibcode = 1970JChEd..47..154R | url=https://escholarship.org/content/qt5mp6r34r/qt5mp6r34r.pdf?t=p0fu3t }}</ref>  

His work in the area of [[economics]] postulated that money was the economic equivalent of the lowest form of [[social entropy]] as described in his work “Teachings on Energy” (''in German'', ''Lehre von der Energie'', 1887[https://archive.org/details/dielehrevondere00helmgoog]).

==Selected works==
* ''Lehre von der Energie'' (Leipzig, 1887) [https://archive.org/details/dielehrevondere00helmgoog]
* ''Grundzüge der mathematischen Chemie'' (1894) [https://books.google.com/books?id=V7BgQAzf8hkC&q=Grundz%C3%BCge+der+mathematischen+Chemie+Helm&pg=PA1]
** ''The principles of mathematical chemistry: The energetics of chemical phenomena'' (New York, 1897) [https://books.google.com/books?id=cyUuAAAAYAAJ&q=The+principles+of+mathematical+chemistry]
* ''Die Energetik'' (Leipzig, 1898)
* ''Die Theorien der Elektrodynamik nach ihrer geschichtlichen Entwicklung'' (Leipzig, 1904) [https://books.google.com/books?id=y-NdHGW9hG8C&dq=Die+Theorien+der+Elektrodynamik+nach+ihrer+geschichtlichen+Entwicklung+helm&pg=PA21]
* ''Die Grundlehren der höheren Mathematik'' (Leipzig, 1910)
